newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-CAPRIATI RALLIES TO BEAT RAYMOND IN CHICAGO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CAPRIATI RALLIES TO BEAT RAYMOND IN CHICAGO.

text.p: Jennifer Capriati, looking more like the top 10 player she was two years ago, rallied to defeat Lisa Raymond 7-5 7-6 (7-1) in the first round of the $450,000 Ameritech Cup tennis tournament on Tuesday.

Capriati, 20, who has spent most of the last two seasons recovering from drug abuse and injury problems, was a late entry to the tournament, replacing Gabriela Sabatini, who unexpectedly announced her retirement.
"I feel my timing has come back," said Capriati, ranked 50th in the world. "I can do more of what I want to do and I'm able to get into the rhythm of my old game."

Capriati rallied in the first set from a 5-3 deficit to break Raymond at love in the next game. Raymond, coming off her first tour singles title at the Bell Challenge in Quebec City, Canada, scored only two points in the final four games as Capriati seemed to find her baseline stroke.

"I missed a ton of forehands but that's when she started to pick it up," said Raymond, 23. "She's hitting the ball great. What surprised me was the way she moved. She moved to the ball a lot better than I thought she would."
In the second set, Raymond nearly broke Capriati's serve in her final three games, but each time, the former Olympic champion rallied with precise deep groundstrokes in the corners.
"It felt good that I could pull it out the close times when I needed to," Capriati said. "I feel my game is getting better each match."
Seventh seed Brenda Schultz-McCarthy defeated Lori McNeil for the first time in five career meetings, 7-6 (7-2) 6-7 (3-7) 6-4 in Tuesday's only match involving a seeded player.
"I look up to her a little bit," said Schultz-McCarthy, ranked 11th in the world. "The first time I played her was in Oklahoma (in 1988) and I was 16 and didn't have a backhand yet."
Schultz-McCarthy, who has a powerful serve, admitted she appreciated the long match because she needed the court time -- she has played on four different indoor surfaces in her last four tournaments.

McNeil, sidelined three months because of injuries, says she just needs to play. Former NBA player and coach John Lucas has been her coach since Wimbledon, hoping, she said, to help me get my confidence back.''

In other first-round matches, Mary Joe Fernandez defeated Meghan Shaugnessy 6-2 6-4, Amy Frazier beat Meilen Tu 6-3 7-5, Linda Wild defeated Kimberly Po 6-2 6-3 and Irina Spirlea beat Marianne Werdel Witmeyer 6-3 6-0.
